Hiscox said on Tuesday that ICWP rose to $4.44bn from $4.05bn a year earlier, with retail premiums up 9.1% in constant currency to $2.25bn as growth strengthened across its UK, European and US operations. The FTSE 100-listed firm also reiterated guidance for 9% constant-currency retail growth for the full year and said its change programme remained on track to deliver a $75m profit and loss benefit in 2026.

posted a sharp fall in annual profits on Tuesday, as challenging conditions hit both its grocery and retail businesses. The owner of fast fashion retailer Primark, as well as a host of grocery brands, including Twinings, Ovaltine and Silver Spoon, saw group revenues soften 1% in the year to 12 September, to £19.6bn, while adjusted operating profits on a constant currency basis were 14% lower, at £1.5bn. Like-for-like sales at Primark were 2.6% weaker over the year, after modest 0.5% uplifts in the UK and Ireland were offset by a 4.7% slide in mainland Europe. In the grocery business, sales improved 2%, after a strong performance by a number of brands and the acquisition Hovis was partially offset by lower sales of US oils. However, AB's sugar business continued to face a number of headwinds, including lower average selling prices, leading to a 9% fall in revenues.

Major indices delivered a mixed performance on Monday, as market participants continued to rotated out of tech stocks and increase exposure to other parts of the economy.
At the close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.41% at 51,983.98, while the S&P 500 shed 0.51% to 7,541.40 and the Nasdaq Composite saw out the session 1.07% weaker at 25,164.32.
